da-circular.evidence: .md:60-72 'Structural reading': reads the numerator 3q²−1 as '3 = number of saturating-genus generation torus knots T(2,3),T(2,5),T(2,7)' and denominator 2q² as 'EM-self-energy halving (Casimir)'. These interpretations are imposed on coefficients that arise purely from the elementary algebra 1+ℏ_q−ℏ_q²/2.
da-circular.notes: The '3' and '2' in (3q²−1)/(2q²) come directly from the Taylor truncation 1+ℏ−½ℏ² (constant 1, linear +1, the ½), i.e. from the chosen truncation order — not from Bring-surface generation counting. Attaching '3 generations' and 'Casimir halving' meaning to these is a post-hoc structural reading, not a derivation; it risks circular significance-assignment. The .md itself flags 'modulo a rigorous first-principles derivation of the ℏ_q−ℏ_q²/2 truncation order' (.md:72), which is honest. Minor — the algebra is correct; only the interpretive overlay is suggestive-not-derived.

But the block ITSELF only proves the elementary algebraic identity (the (3q²−1)/(2q²) rewrite); the meson-ratio closure, [3]_q·[4]_q fusion, and α_em=q·[9]_q·[10]_q are imported from other props, and the truncation order 1+ℏ−½ℏ² is admittedly unproved (.md:72).
da-overclaim.notes: The proved content is just rational-function algebra (the .md 'Mathematical Novelty' note, line 75, is candid about this). The significance section presents the full m_K²/m_π² closure as 'derived / no fitted integers', but the choice of truncation order (why exactly 1+ℏ−½ℏ², i.e. why second-order with coefficient −½) is the load-bearing modeling choice and is explicitly NOT derived ('modulo a rigorous first-principles derivation of the truncation order'). Calling the assembled ratio 'derived (no fitted integers)' while the truncation order is hand-chosen is an overclaim — the −½ℏ² truncation IS effectively a modeling degree of freedom. Major because 'no fitted integers / framework-derived' is exactly the production-vs-exploratory claim the canonical-watcher polices.

da-hidden-dof.evidence: .md:72 admits the result holds 'modulo a rigorous first-principles derivation of the ℏ_q − ℏ_q²/2 truncation order'. The truncation 1 + ℏ_q − ℏ_q²/2 (keep to O(ℏ²), coefficient −1/2 on the quadratic) is the choice that produces the exact coefficients 3 and the −½; a different truncation (e.g. +½ℏ², or O(ℏ³)) changes the numerator/denominator.
da-hidden-dof.notes: The truncation order/coefficient is an undisclosed-as-such free choice presented post-hoc as structurally meaningful (3 generations, Casimir 2). It has no stated canonical-chain origin — the .md concedes the derivation is pending. This is a hidden modeling DOF dressed as derived numerology (3, 2). Major per the framework's own Rule-14 / production-vs-exploratory discipline: an h^k truncation whose order is chosen to match must be flagged, not presented as 'no fitted integers'.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: accept-the-lemma-revise-the-significance. referee_argument: The proved object — the rational-function identity 1+ℏ_q−ℏ_q²/2 = (3q²−1)/(2q²) — is correct, generic over any field, and faithfully formalized sorry-free (no Lean/narrative divergence; da-false-claim/da-vacuous/da-lean pass). The block's weakness is entirely in the significance/structural-reading prose. Strongest objection (da-overclaim + da-hidden-dof): the .md presents the assembled m_K²/m_π² = [3]_q[4]_q + (α_em/π)(3q²−1)/(2q²) as 'a single closed-form derived expression' with 'no fitted integers / framework-derived', yet the truncation order 1+ℏ−½ℏ² (which fixes the coefficients 3 and ½) is admittedly NOT derived ('modulo a rigorous first-principles derivation of the truncation order', .md:72). That truncation choice is a hidden modeling DOF, and the post-hoc reading of '3' as three fermion generations and '2q²' as Casimir EM halving is suggestive numerology, not derivation. Required revision: scope the significance section as 'a candidate closed form consistent with the meson ratio, pending derivation of the truncation order', and avoid the 'no fitted integers / derived' framing until the truncation order is pinned; add a reproducible witness for the claimed sub-ppm match. The elementary identity itself is publication-ready.
